(1) the loss landscape of deep half-activated networks is connected, (2) the level sets become exponentially more curvy, and (3) the energy landscape of deep half activated networks has a radically more complicated topology than that of deep linear networks.

(i) half-rectified networks have a very different topological structure compared to linear networks; and (ii) the geometry of the landscape of half-rectified network optimization is controlled by the smoothness of data and the amount of model overparametrization.

half-rectification makes a deep network’s landscape fundamentally more complex than its linear counterpart and that, in spite of this complexity, it is not possible to construct a local minimum that is significantly worse than the global one, as long as the model is over-parameterized.
